description: Interactive map with tile, UDF and SQL layers.

basemap.description: Mapbox style URL (e.g. "mapbox://styles/mapbox/dark-v11", "mapbox://styles/mapbox/light-v11", "mapbox://styles/mapbox/satellite-streets-v12") or "blank" for a plain background. Omit it so the map follows the app light/dark theme; when the viewer picks a basemap in the switcher it is written into this prop, so only set it when a fixed basemap is wanted.

layerBlending.description: How the data layers blend where they overlap, one setting for every layer (kepler.gl's Layer blending, same values): "normal" (the default, plain alpha), "additive" (overlaps grow brighter; reads best on a dark basemap) or "subtractive" (overlaps grow darker). Layers draw into the basemap, so the blend mixes with its pixels too. The selection outline and failed-tile squares stay normal, and raster layers stay normal under subtractive (their transparent pixels would black out the basemap). Picking it in the sidebar's Layers tab writes it here; normal removes it.

centerLng.description: Map centre longitude (defaults to -98). Setting centerLng or centerLat turns auto-fit off unless autoFit is set explicitly.

centerLat.description: Map centre latitude (defaults to 39.5). Setting centerLng or centerLat turns auto-fit off unless autoFit is set explicitly.

zoom.description: Initial zoom level; only used when auto-fit is off.

autoFit.description: Fly to the loaded data once on first load: inline GeoJSON plus every visible udf / sql row layer. Defaults to true, or false when centerLng/centerLat is set (an explicit camera wins). Later pans, re-runs and basemap switches leave the camera alone, and a camera the viewer left behind wins. Tile layers never report bounds. When off the map opens at centerLng/centerLat/zoom.

type.description: Layer type. Omit it to detect from the data: an image → raster (tiles from a tile UDF, else one image placed at the bounds the run returned or was sent), an H3 cell column → h3, start/end lat-lng pairs → arc, one lat-lng pair → scatterplot, a geometry column → geojson. The detected type and columns are written into this config once known. All types render through deck.gl. geojson: polygons/lines/points from inline data, sql or udf rows (deck-geojson is an alias of geojson; prefer geojson). h3: hexagons from h3Column. scatterplot: point circles. heatmap: point density. arc: source→target arcs. raster: tiles from tileUrl or a udf with tile: true, else a single image from a udf. mvt: tiles from tileUrl, or from udf with tile: true. fused-hex: H3 tiles queried from a Fused server's ERA5, gridMET or /h3/query endpoints (see source); it is never detected, so set it explicitly. For your own data: partition it with fused.h3.partition, register it with fused.h3.index, then set source {path, overview: {}} and h3Column. Row tiles load from the layer's zoom floor (default zoom 7) and a zoomed-out overview of the whole dataset draws below it.

tileUrl.description: Tile URL template with {x}/{y}/{z} placeholders (mvt, raster, tiled h3)

minZoom.description: Minimum zoom for tiled layers (mvt, raster, tiled h3)

maxZoom.description: Maximum zoom for tiled layers (mvt, raster, tiled h3)

zoomOffset.description: Zoom offset for tiled layers (useful for hex tile generalization)

maxRequests.description: Maximum parallel tile requests for tiled layers

autoRetry.description: Retry failed tiles automatically: a few fetch attempts on transient errors, and a refetch when a failed tile scrolls back into view. Default true. Set false to make a tile fail after one attempt and stay failed until Retry.

bounds.description: Lock a udf tile layer (tile: true) drawn as geojson or deck-geojson to these bounds [minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]: the UDF runs once with bounds passed as a parameter (a JSON string "[w, s, e, n]", like the legacy single-viewport run) and the result renders as one static layer, with no per-tile runs and no refetch on pan or zoom. A sql on the layer runs on that one result while locked, and over the tiles in view otherwise. Ignored by other layers: other types (h3, scatterplot, arc, heatmap, raster, mvt) keep their tiles.

sourceLayer.description: Source layer name for MVT tiles (defaults to 'default')

data.description: Inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection, or one {{name}} placeholder naming a canvas SQL source: an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name (offered by Add layer and wired by an edge automatically), or another map's layer id (draw the edge from that map yourself). The source's rows are read from DuckDB as they are (no UDF runs; its loading and errors show on the layer; it re-queries when the widget fetches again), and the edge from that node to this one grants access, as for a UDF. Add sql to query them ({{source}} or {{name}} reads the rows). Row layers only (geojson, h3, scatterplot, heatmap, arc, or type omitted to detect from the rows): not with tile, udf or tileUrl, nor on raster, mvt or fused-hex. Example: "{{h3_rows}}" with h3Column "hex".

udf.description: UDF placeholder, e.g. {{my_udf}}, {{my_udf?param=value}} or {{my_udf?param=$param_name}}. The UDF is run directly (no share token needed) and re-run when it or a referenced $param_name changes: the whole result as rows for geojson/deck layers, or per tile when tile is true (a sql then queries the tiles in view). An input in the same widget (slider, number-input, with a defaultValue) can drive it; only the UDF → widget edge is needed. Combine with sql to query the result (the tiles in view when tile is true). Mutually exclusive with tileUrl.

tile.description: With udf: run the UDF per XYZ tile (raster → PNG bitmaps, h3 → hexagons, geojson → vector features). Required when type is mvt and the source is a udf. Without it a raster udf layer runs once and draws one image at the bounds the run returned (`image, bounds`) or was sent (the map view at the time of the run, for a UDF with a bounds parameter; moving the map later does not run it again). Tiled layers never auto-fit and ignore the whole-result size limit.

sql.description: DuckDB SQL query with {{name}} placeholders: a UDF result, or a canvas SQL source (an h3-query or sql-runner widget's name, another map's layer id) read from DuckDB with no UDF run. Rows are converted to GeoJSON for rendering. On a tiled layer (udf with tile: true, or fused-hex) the query runs once over the rows of every tile loaded in the current view, reading them as {{source}}, which takes no ?params (a udf layer may also write its own {{udf_name}}, bare or with exactly its own ?params), and runs again as the view moves (pan, zoom), the query changes or a $param changes; no tile is refetched. WHERE, computed columns, GROUP BY, aggregates, LIMIT, ORDER BY and USING SAMPLE apply to the whole view (before a fused-hex reduce); only a single SELECT (a WITH is fine) over {{source}} runs (no UNION, several statements, other UDFs or joins), and its result must keep the cell column (h3, fused-hex) or the geometry columns (vector layers). raster, mvt and tileUrl layers take no sql.

filters.description: Feature filters applied on the client: range filters on numeric properties, category filters on any property.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound, or a `$param` holding one

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none

max.description: Inclusive upper bound, or a `$param` holding one

anyOf.description: A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none
A canvas parameter reference such as `$day_min`; the filter reads its value live and is inactive while the parameter has none

values.description: Values to keep (empty keeps every feature), or a `$param` holding the list

geometryColumn.description: Column containing the geometry: GeoJSON strings (use ST_AsGeoJSON in SQL), GeoJSON objects, or WKB blobs as stored by GeoDataFrame outputs. Defaults to 'geometry'.

h3Column.description: Column containing H3 hex indexes (h3 layer type). Auto-detected from common names (hex, h3, ...) when omitted.

latColumn.description: Column for latitude (point data). Defaults to 'lat'.

lngColumn.description: Column for longitude (point data). Defaults to 'lng'.

startLatColumn.description: Column for the arc start latitude (arc layer type).

startLngColumn.description: Column for the arc start longitude (arc layer type).

endLatColumn.description: Column for the arc end latitude (arc layer type).

endLngColumn.description: Column for the arc end longitude (arc layer type).

tooltip.description: Show tooltip on hover. true = all properties, string[] = specific properties. Off for data rows when unset. A fused-hex overview cell always shows its hover (cell, rows, rows in window) unless this is false.

legend.description: Show color legend for this layer. true = auto title, {title} = custom title. Only applies when fillColor or lineColor is data-driven.

source.description: fused-hex only: the server endpoint and query each XYZ tile's bbox is sent to. For your own data, set path to an indexed folder and overview to {}; the layer then also needs h3Column. Example: {path: 's3://bucket/indexed/', overview: {}} with h3Column 'hex' and style.fillColor {type: 'continuous', attr: 'temp'}.

endpoint.description: Bbox query endpoint on a Fused server: a full URL or a path relative to the current server root. Supported: /retrieve/era5/daily/bbox, /retrieve/era5/hourly/bbox, /retrieve/gridmet/bbox and /h3/query. Defaults to /h3/query when path is set.

path.description: Indexed dataset location, e.g. s3://bucket/indexed/data/. Sets the endpoint to /h3/query when none is given. Needs the layer's h3Column (the location's indexed space column, 'hex' for what fused.h3.partition writes). The folder must be hex-sorted H3 parquet that fused.h3.partition wrote and fused.h3.index registered for your team (run partition, then index; pass chunk_res_offset to partition for the chunk-level overview). Not used by the retrieve endpoints, which serve a fixed dataset.

dateMin.description: Inclusive start of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

dateMax.description: Inclusive end of the time window (ISO date or datetime). Required for the retrieve endpoints.

variables.description: Measurement columns to fetch. Defaults to the attributes the style, tooltip and filters name, or every column when none do.

reduce.description: How each hex's rows across the time window collapse to one value: latest (default) or first keep one time step; mean, min, max and sum aggregate every numeric variable and add count, date_min and date_max.

hour.description: Hourly datasets only: keep rows for this hour of the day before reducing.

timeColumn.description: Column holding each row's time, used to order rows for latest/first. Defaults to 'date' for the retrieve endpoints; set it for /h3/query datasets.

limit.description: Server row cap per tile request (the endpoint's `limit`)

maxRowGroups.description: Server row group cap per tile request (`max_row_groups`)

maxRanges.description: Retrieve endpoints only: cell ranges the bbox cover may use (`max_ranges`). Higher values cover each tile more tightly, so fewer rows outside it are read.

minZoom.description: The overview needs the layer's zoom floor above this (default 3). It draws at every zoom below the floor, where row tiles start.

extent.description: [west, south, east, north] the overview looks up files in, with west < east (boxes crossing the antimeridian are not supported). Row tiles are also confined to it: none are requested outside it. Cells are drawn only inside it, in the overview and in rows, by cell centre. Defaults to the whole world.

overview.description: Zoomed-out view below the layer's zoom floor, drawn from one request, so `overview: {}` is all it takes. Each cell is a file's H3 cell (file level) or, when the location was partitioned chunk-aligned (fused.h3.partition with chunk_res_offset) and has at most 100,000 distinct chunk cells, one row-group chunk (chunk level). The server picks the level; ERA5 and gridMET are always file level. Default at both levels: cells fill light by row count with grey outlines, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only their row counts, never column values, at either level. Hovering a cell shows it, its row count and the rows the current date window reads. Available for the ERA5 and gridMET retrieve endpoints and /h3/query. style.overview overrides the colours.

loader.description: How each tile's row groups are read. server (the default) has the server read them and answer Parquet pages. browser reads the row groups from object storage in the browser, from a plan the server answers (/h3/query with format=browser); it needs an execution environment, and a share link without one fails. auto tries browser and falls back to server when the plan is refused or the browser loader cannot start.

maxChunks.description: Browser and auto loaders only: most chunks (storage range requests) the browser may fetch for one tile page. Defaults to 1000. A tile whose plan needs more is not loaded and the layer shows a warning naming the value to set here.

fillColor.description: Fill color (source colour for arc, weight attr for heatmap): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or data-driven {type:"continuous", attr, domain?:[min,max], palette?, steps?, reverse?, nullColor?, scaleType?:"quantize"|"quantile"} | {type:"categorical", attr, colors?:{value:"#hex"}, palette?, nullColor?}. See the component description for palette names.

lineColor.description: Stroke color (target colour for arc): [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] array, CSS string, or the same data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} object as fillColor.

coverage.description: H3 hex coverage 0-1 (1 = no gap, 0.8 = small gaps). Defaults to 1 for fused-hex layers, 0.9 for other hex layers.

elevationAttr.description: Feature property to use for extrusion height

overview.description: fused-hex only, optional: overrides how the overview cells (source.overview) draw; leave it out for the defaults, which need no setting. Defaults, at both levels: light fill by row count with #afafaf outlines at opacity 0.35, not coloured by the layer's colour. Cells carry only row counts (row_count_total, row_count_window), so a colour can only be data-driven by those; hovering a cell shows it and its row counts. Example: {fillColor: [255, 140, 0], opacity: 0.5, lineWidth: 0}. null clears a configured block (a layer switched out of fused-hex).

fillColor.description: Unset or "auto": a light fill by row_count_total at both levels, so the overview does not read as data coloured by a column. A single colour fills the cells; null draws no fill; "inherit" takes the layer's fillColor (a single colour is used as is; a data-driven one falls back to the row-count fill, since cells carry no column values); or a data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} over the only cell properties: row_count_total (rows in the cell's files or chunk) and row_count_window (rows the current date window reads). Any other attr falls back to the row-count fill.

opacity.description: Opacity 0-1 of the overview cells, fill and outline alike. Defaults to 0.35; with fillColor "inherit" of a single colour at the chunk level, the layer's own opacity.

lineColor.description: Unset or "auto": #afafaf at both levels. A single colour outlines the cells; "inherit" takes the layer's lineColor (a data-driven one falls back to #afafaf); or a data-driven {type:"continuous"|"categorical", attr, ...} over the same cell properties as fillColor.

lineWidth.description: Overview cell stroke width in pixels. Defaults to 1 at both levels; 0 draws no outline.

stat.description: No longer used and ignored: overview cells carry no column statistics. Accepted so saved configs that set it still load.

showCoordinates.description: Show the map centre's latitude, longitude and zoom under the scale bar; a click copies them

showBasemapSwitcher.description: Offer the dark/light/satellite basemap choice: the sidebar's Base map tab, or a floating toggle when showSidebar is false

showLegend.description: Show color legend for layers with data-driven colors

showLayerPanel.description: Show the floating layer panel for toggling visibility and opacity when showSidebar is false (the sidebar's layer list covers this otherwise)

showSidebar.description: Show the sidebar toggle for editing layer style, filters and SQL at runtime. On your own canvas the edits are written into this config as you make them (undo with Cmd/Ctrl+Z in the sidebar or the code editor); elsewhere they are runtime overrides you can copy into the config.

param.description: Canvas parameter name to sync viewport bounds [west, south, east, north]

autoSendDebounceMs.description: Debounce ms for auto-send (0 = send on every move)

clickParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the properties of the last clicked feature

hoverParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the properties of the feature under the cursor, in the same shape as clickParam (only the layer's tooltip fields when it lists them). Sent at most once per animation frame and only when the hovered feature changes; a new feature is not sent while the map is dragged. Cleared (removed, like fused.params.set(name, null)) when the cursor leaves every feature. Session state: not saved with the canvas.

selectParam.description: Canvas parameter that receives the current selection: shift+drag draws a box (the map dims outside it), shift+click toggles one feature, Escape or a plain click on the map clears. Value: { layer, key, ids, count, bbox, mode, truncated }. Session state: not saved with the canvas. bbox is the [west, south, east, north] envelope of the drawn box (null for click selections) and is the selection for a box: filter rows by it. ids are the `selectKey` values of every feature drawn in the box, with no cap; truncated is always false. Another widget or an HTML page can write it too: null or an empty selection ({ mode: "none" } or { ids: [], bbox: null }) clears the outline and dimming, and { bbox: [west, south, east, north] } draws that box (its ids are not re-picked; west must be less than east). Only nodes wired to the map by an edge in either direction (or the page it is embedded in) are heard, and only writes made while the map is mounted. Ids without a bbox do not change what the map shows.

sourceParam.description: Canvas parameter that signals when a layer's `{{layer_id}}` rows change, so a page can re-query instead of polling. Value: { [layerId]: { version, loading, rows, error } }. Re-run fused.query when version changes (compare with !==, not >). version is 0 while the layer has no rows, loading is true while newer rows are built, rows is the row count when known (else null), error is the last build error. Session state: not saved with the canvas.

selectKey.description: Feature property published as each selected feature's id in selectParam. Defaults to the cell column on hex layers, else `id`.

stateParam.description: Canvas parameter that mirrors the map's runtime state (camera, layer type, style, filters, SQL overrides) so other widgets can read it. It is saved with the canvas and restored on reload. On your own canvas layer edits are written into this config as you make them, so the parameter mostly carries the camera. The camera is `view`: { centerLng, centerLat, zoom, bearing, pitch, width, height }, written when a pan, zoom, rotate or tilt gesture ends (not during it). zoom is exact (6 decimals, Web Mercator with 512 px tiles), bearing and pitch are degrees, and width and height are the map canvas size in CSS pixels at that moment, so a page can project lng/lat to pixels; width and height are ignored when the camera is restored.

style.description: Inline CSS styles as a plain CSS string
